speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin understanding your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you recall any specific trauma or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The connection between your recent camping trip in Minnesota, the self-resolving knee pain, and now this wrist infection with fever is concerning for Lyme carditis or disseminated Lyme disease; were you bitten by a tick during that trip? Additionally, given your sexual history, could you describe the appearance and location of the skin lesions?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP; REQUEST TEST: Lyme Serology (ELISA/Western Blot); REQUEST TEST: Syphilis Serology (RPR/FTA-ABS)
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_photos_of_skin_lesions

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: Not available; CRP: Not available; Lyme Serology: Not available; Syphilis Serology: Not available; Dermatology Photos: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lyme Arthritis (Lyme Disease) presenting with tenosynovitis and characteristic erythema migrans-like lesions.

The elevated WBC confirms an active infection, and the history of self-resolving knee pain followed by wrist involvement after a Minnesota camping trip is classic for disseminated Lyme disease. The painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists are highly suggestive of early disseminated Lyme, distinct from syphilis. Given the strong clinical evidence, I will proceed with treatment without further questioning.
